title: $42 an Hour Is How Much a Year? (2026)
metaDescription: $42/hour is $87,360 a year at 40 hrs/week — $7,280 monthly, $3,360.00 biweekly. See overtime pay tables and a 2026 federal take-home estimate.

hero.lede: Full time at 40 hours a week, 52 weeks a year (2,080 hours). Below: every pay-period equivalent, overtime tables at time-and-a-half, and a 2026 federal-only take-home estimate.

shortAnswer.heading: How much is $42 an hour per year?
shortAnswer.html: $42 an hour is $87,360 a year at 40 hours a week for 52 weeks (2,080 hours). That's $1,680.00 a week, $3,360.00 biweekly, and $7,280.00 a month gross. After estimated federal income tax and FICA, a single filer keeps about $70,288 — and steady overtime at $63.00/hour raises the total fast.

sections.title: What $42/hour adds up to per period.
sections.note: Gross (pre-tax) figures assuming paid hours every week of the year. Unpaid time off reduces them proportionally.

sections.title: $42 an hour in 2026, in plain numbers.
paragraphs: At $42 an hour, a full-time year — 40 hours a week for 52 weeks, with no unpaid time off — grosses $87,360. That's $1,680.00 a week, $3,360.00 per biweekly paycheck, and about $7,280.00 a month before taxes.

Measured against the middle of the U.S. labor market, $42/hour is about 34% above the U.S. median full-time wage — the BLS median works out to about $31.28/hour ($1,251/week, BLS, Q2 2026). The big lever for hourly earners is overtime: every OT hour pays $63.00 at time-and-a-half.

sections.title: Overtime at $63.00/hour changes the math quickly.
sections.note: Overtime rows assume time-and-a-half (1.5 × $42 = $63.00) on hours past 40, every week of the year — the FLSA baseline for non-exempt workers.

sections.title: From $87,360 gross to take-home.
sections.note: Single filer, standard deduction, no state/local income tax, credits, or pre-tax benefits. Actual checks vary.

sections.title: What a single filer actually keeps.
paragraphs: Federally, this wage puts a single filer in the 22% marginal bracket for 2026: $87,360 gross less the $16,100 standard deduction is $71,260 taxable, generating $10,389 of income tax (11.9% effective). Add $6,683 of FICA and estimated take-home is $70,288/year, or $5,857.31/month.

faq.q: How much is $42 an hour per year?
faq.a: $42 an hour is $87,360 a year at full time — 40 hours a week for 52 weeks (2,080 hours). At 30 hours a week it comes to $65,520, and with 10 hours of weekly overtime it reaches about $120,120.

faq.q: How much is $42 an hour biweekly?
faq.a: A standard 80-hour biweekly period at $42/hour grosses $3,360.00. After estimated federal income tax and FICA for a single filer, roughly $2,703.38 remains per check, before state taxes.

faq.q: How much is $42 an hour after taxes?
faq.a: On $87,360 of annual wages, a single filer taking the 2026 standard deduction pays about $10,389 of federal income tax plus $6,683 of FICA, keeping roughly $70,288 a year — about $33.79 per hour worked. State and local taxes reduce this further where they apply.

faq.q: How much is $42 an hour with overtime?
faq.a: Overtime pays time-and-a-half: $63.00 per hour past 40 in a week. A steady 50-hour week earns $2,310.00 weekly — $120,120 a year, $32,760 more than the straight 40-hour year.

faq.q: Is $42 an hour a good wage in 2026?
faq.a: $42/hour annualizes to $87,360, which is about 34% above the U.S. median full-time wage — the BLS median for full-time workers is $1,251/week (about $31.28/hour, BLS, Q2 2026). Local cost of living, benefits, and schedule stability matter as much as the rate itself.

methodology: Annualization is straight arithmetic: $42 × 2,080 hours (40 hours × 52 weeks) = $87,360, with daily/weekly/biweekly/monthly rows derived the same way. No unpaid leave is assumed.
Overtime rows use the FLSA non-exempt baseline of 1.5× base pay ($63.00/hour) on hours over 40 per week, sustained all 52 weeks.
The take-home estimate uses 2026 federal brackets for a single filer with the $16,100 standard deduction plus employee FICA (7.65%). It excludes state/local tax, credits, and pre-tax benefits.
Median-wage comparison: BLS median usual weekly earnings, full-time workers, $1,251/week (BLS, Q2 2026).
Educational estimates only — not tax, legal, or financial advice.
